questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Observe the following statements
i. The dipole moment of $\mathrm{NH}_3$ is higher than the dipole moment of $\mathrm{NF}_3$.
ii. The dipole moment of chloroform is zero.
iii. Covalent bond character in $\mathrm{NaCl}$ is more compared to $\mathrm{CuCl}$.
questions.solution:
Only statement (i) is correct.
- i. The dipole moment of \(\mathrm{NH}_3\) is higher than the dipole moment of \(\mathrm{NF}_3\). This is correct. In \(\mathrm{NH}_3\), the bond dipoles of the three \(\mathrm{N}-\mathrm{H}\) bonds and the lone pair on nitrogen all point in the same general direction, adding up to a larger net dipole moment. In \(N F_3\), the bond dipoles of the three N-F bonds point towards the highly electronegative fluorine atoms, while the lone pair dipole points away. These dipoles oppose each other, resulting in a much smaller net dipole moment.
- if. The dipole moment of chloroform is zero. This is incorrect. Chloroform (\(\mathrm{CHCl}_3\)) is a tetrahedral molecule with three highly electronegative chlorine atoms and one less electronegative hydrogen atom. The bond dipoles do not cancel each other out, resulting in a significant net dipole moment.
- iii. Covalent bond character in NaCl is more compared to CuCl . This is incorrect. According to Fajan's rules, a smaller cation with a pseudo-noble gas configuration (like \(C u^{+}\)) has a greater polarizing power than a cation with a noble gas configuration (like \(\mathrm{Na}^{+}\)). This increased polarizing power leads to a greater covalent character. Therefore, CuCl is more covalent than NaCl.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Assertion (A) : Reaction of 1-butene with $\mathrm{HBr}$ gives 1-bromobutane as major product.
Reason $(\mathrm{R})$ : Addition of $\mathrm{HBr}$ to unsymmetrical alkenes proceeds according to Markovnikov's rule
The correct answer is
options: (A) and (R) are correct, (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
(A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.solution:
- Assertion (A): "Reaction of 1-butene with HBr gives 1-bromobutane as a major product." This is incorrect. According to Markovnikov's rule, the hydrogen atom of HBr adds to the carbon atom of the double bond that already has more hydrogen atoms. Thus, in the reaction of 1butene (\(\mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CH}=\mathrm{CH}_2\)) with HBr, the hydrogen adds to \(\mathrm{CH}_2\) and the bromine adds to the second carbon atom (\(C H\)) to give 2-bromobutane as the major product.
- Reason (R): "Addition of HBr to unsymmetrical alkenes proceeds according to Markovnikov's rule." This is correct. Markovnikov's rule states that for an electrophilic addition reaction of a protic acid (like HBr) to an unsymmetrical alkene, the proton adds to the carbon with more hydrogen atoms, and the halide adds to the more substituted carbon.
The assertion is incorrect, but the reason is correct. Therefore, the answer is (4) (A) is not correct but (R) is correct.

questions.q: A body is projected at $t=0$ with a velocity $10 \mathrm{~ms}^{-1}$ at an angle of $60^{\circ}$ with the horizontal. The radius of curvature of its trajectory at $t=1 s$ is $R$. Neglecting air resistance and taking acceleration due to gravity $g=10 \mathrm{~ms}^{-2}$, the value of $R$ is :
questions.solution: Given Data: Initial velocity, $u=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$ Angle of projection, $\theta=60^{\circ}$ Radius of curvature at $t=1 s$ is $R$ Acceleration due to gravity, $g=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$ Finding the radius of curvature: Resolving the velocity into $x$ and $y$ components, at any time $t$ \begin{aligned} & v_x=u \cos 60^{\circ}=10 \times \frac{1}{2} \\ & v_x=5 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s} \\ & v_y=u \sin 60^{\circ}+a t=\frac{10 \sqrt{3}}{2}-10 t \\ & v_y=|5 \sqrt{3}-10 t| \end{aligned} $$ \\ At $t=1 s$ v_y=|5 \sqrt{3}-10| Angle made by body with respect to horizontal axis at $t=1 \mathrm{~s}$ \begin{aligned} & \tan \alpha=\left|\frac{v_y}{v_x}\right|=\left|\frac{5 \sqrt{3}-10}{5}\right|, \\ & \tan \alpha==|\sqrt{3}-2| \\ & \alpha=\tan ^{-1}(|\sqrt{3}-2|)=15^{\circ} \end{aligned} The radius of curvature same as range at time $t$, which is given by \begin{aligned} R & =\frac{v^2}{g \cos \alpha}=\frac{v_x^2+v_y^2}{g \cos \alpha} \\ R & =\frac{5^2+(5 \sqrt{3}-10)^2}{10 \times \cos 15^o} \\ R & =\frac{25+75+100-100 \sqrt{3}}{10 \times \cos 15^{\circ}} \\ R & =\frac{26.79}{9.65}=2.77 \\ R & =2.77 m \approx 2.8 m \end{aligned} Hence, option $C$ is correct
